Research Scientist, Machine Learning & Signal Processing [Technical Leadership]
Research Scientist, Machine Learning & Signal Processing [Technical Leadership]
Burlingame, CA
Machine Learning
+ 1 more
Apply now
Meta is seeking a Research Scientist to lead applied AI initiatives at the intersection of wearable technology and AI modeling of diverse sensors, including EMG, motion sensors, audio, and video. In this role, you will define and drive the scientific agenda for a team of AI research scientists, computational neuroscientists, and machine learning engineers, shaping the direction of next-generation AI capabilities that power Meta's wearable devices and health-focused experiences. You will operate at the frontier of AI research for human-computer interaction, translating scientific advances in biosignal interpretation into scalable systems with measurable product impact.
Research Scientist, Machine Learning & Signal Processing [Technical Leadership] Responsibilities
Define and drive the research strategy and roadmap for an AI research team focused on wearables, EMG, and wearable sensors, balancing applied machine learning investments with product deliverables
Lead the development of novel AI architectures, training methodologies, and evaluation frameworks for EMG signal processing, sensor fusion, and wearable device intelligence
Establish technical direction for the team by identifying high-impact research problems in sensor signal interpretation and wearable AI, scoping projects, and aligning efforts to broader organizational priorities
Build and grow a high-performing team of AI researchers and engineers through hiring, mentorship, and structured development of research talent
Collaborate with product, engineering, and hardware partners to translate research breakthroughs in EMG and sensing into production wearable systems at Meta's scale
Drive promising research outcomes from research to production, ensuring innovative findings are successfully transitioned into scalable wearable products and features
Communicate research findings and strategic recommendations to organizational leaders and cross-functional stakeholders through written reports, presentations, and design reviews
Foster a team culture that values scientific rigor, engineering craft, and responsible AI development in alignment with Meta's values and compliance standards
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience
12+ years of experience in AI or machine learning research, including experience leading research teams or large-scale research programs
Experience establishing research strategy and roadmaps with demonstrated impact on AI systems or products at scale
Experience attracting, developing, and retaining research talent, including building leadership pipelines through internal development and external hiring
Track record of executing cross-functional AI research initiatives from ideation through deployment, including managing dependencies across engineering, product, and data science teams
Experience communicating complex AI research directions and technical decisions to both technical and non-technical audiences through written and verbal formats
Preferred Qualifications
Experience publishing AI, machine learning, or biosignal processing research in peer-reviewed venues such as NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, IEEE EMBC, or similar venues
Experience leading research in one or more specialized domains, such as EMG signal processing, wearable computing, health sensors, human-computer interaction, or physiological signal analysis
About Meta
Meta builds technologies that help people connect, find communities, and grow businesses. When Facebook launched in 2004, it changed the way people connect. Apps like Messenger, Instagram and WhatsApp further empowered billions around the world. Now, Meta is moving beyond 2D screens toward immersive experiences like augmented and virtual reality to help build the next evolution in social technology. People who choose to build their careers by building with us at Meta help shape a future that will take us beyond what digital connection makes possible today—beyond the constraints of screens, the limits of distance, and even the rules of physics.
